<1>Account details:</1> your email address and, if you use Google sign-in, the name and email Google shares with us. If you choose a password, it is stored only in encrypted, one-way form. If you turn on text reminders, your cell phone number, used only to text you deadline reminders.
<1>Basic technical data:</1> sign-in times, device and browser type, and error logs, used to keep the service secure and working.
<1>Family details:</1> your family name, and for each student their first name, birth date, grade, state and the permissions you choose.
<1>Inside your family:</1> the parent who owns the account sees everything in it. A student sees and does only what their parent allows.
<1>Planning details you add:</1> such as courses, grades, test scores, colleges and scholarships you are interested in, and deadlines.

<1>Service providers</1> who host and run ScholarTasks for us under contract: Supabase (database and sign-in), Vercel (website hosting), Resend (email delivery), Twilio (text reminders, only if you turn them on), Anthropic (the Claude AI behind AI help, only when you use an AI feature and have allowed AI help) and Google (only if you choose Google sign-in).
<1>Text messages:</1> we never sell or share your phone number or your agreement to get texts with anyone for their marketing. Your number is used only to send the reminders you turned on.
<1>When required by law,</1> or to protect someone's safety.

A parent or guardian creates the family account. A student gets their own sign-in only at 13 or older, and joins only with a code their parent creates. A parent may add a child aged 10 to 12 in grades 6 to 8 to their own account and use ScholarTasks with them; the child has no sign-in, and nothing about them is sent to an AI service until they turn 13. We do not knowingly collect information directly from children under 13. If you believe a child under 13 has given us information, email <1>{SUPPORTEMAIL}</1> and we will delete it.

ScholarTasks helps families plan for college, scholarships and financial aid. This policy explains what we collect, why, who can see it, and the choices you have. What we collect

When a family connects to their school, the school's counselors see only what the family chose to share, and the family can stop sharing at any time. When a student applies in the app for a school's own local scholarship, only that school's counselors see the application, and only what the family chose to send. A school may upload a class list (names, grades and contact emails) only after signing our student data agreement. We use it only to help that school invite and support its students, never for advertising, and we delete it 45 days after the agreement ends.
